gap: No result ChatGPT got states how long the Aiper EcoSurfer S2 runs on a full battery with no sun at all: 100% ÷ 3.46%/h (The Hook Up's overnight drain test) = about 29 h, which is about 83% of the 35 h Aiper claims.
standout_why: I compared against The Hook Up's test page and its recommendations page (both cited) and RobotDoorstep (cited). The Hook Up test page already gives the sun-hours each robot needs to run nonstop (Beatbot iSkim 6.6 h, Aiper 5.7 h, YouSky 11 h, Wavio 23.2 h) and the Aiper's 3.46%/h overnight drain. That is the core figure for this angle, and a cited rival already has it. What they lack: the drain turned into hours with no sun, a check of that against the maker's 35 h claim, and any cost per watt of solar panel. RobotDoorstep lists panel watts (iSkim 24 W, F1 33 W) but does no math with them, and says it has not tested the robots.
decides: It backs ChatGPT's 'limited sun' pick for the Aiper: on The Hook Up's numbers it needs the fewest sun-hours to run nonstop (5.7 h) and lasts about 29 h after a cloudy day. But it also shows the rated 35 h overstates real runtime by about 17%. The WYBOT F1 gets the most panel per dollar ($9.09/W against about $14.13/W for the iSkim). Nobody has measured its drain, though, so there is no evidence it can run nonstop. It should stay a value option, not the 'never plug in' pick. Not enough here to change the overall pick (Beatbot iSkim).
